text:
The Stars have had a week worth framing. Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points, every one of them in a Dallas sweater, and the team around him has won five straight. Jake Oettinger capped the run by stopping all 33 Pittsburgh shots in a 1-0 win on Saturday, his league-best fifth shutout. Tonight Nashville, three points back in the Central, comes to try to end the streak.

Here is the part of the streak the scoreboard doesn't tell you. Dallas took only 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) across those five wins, and the goaltending saved 8.5 goals more than expected along the way. Oettinger is at +12.4 for the season and +4.7 over his last five starts, with a .914 save rate against hard shots. That is real skill, and the Stars lean on it hard: their +9 goal difference rests on only +4.0 expected. They also take 4.1 penalties a game, which is a lot of rope to hand a power play. Wyatt Johnston has four goals in a five-game point streak.

Nashville won the first meeting, 2-1 on Oct. 3, in a game the chances called close to even. The Predators are a coin flip of a team at five on five (48%), lifted by Juuse Saros at +8.9 saved above expected after a rough last season. Steven Stamkos is on a five-game point streak. Jonathan Marchessault has three points in two games since returning from injury, and Ryan O'Reilly's name keeps turning up in trade talk. Mavrik Bourque plays his first game back in Dallas after 156 games as a Star, still looking for his first goal of the season after 19 games on 4.0 expected goals.

Our numbers have Dallas at 3.10 expected goals and Nashville at 2.63, with Saros and Oettinger in net. Two of the league's better goalies this season, one team whose results run ahead of its play: it's a fair test of how much of the Stars' run is theirs to keep.
headline: Benn's milestone glow, Oettinger's wall, and Nashville at the door
